_note: Every arm sees byte-identical input. Interlocutor turns are scripted rather than generated, so a conversation cannot diverge on what was said to it -- only on what the persona replies.

My dear Darwin,

I have been reading your book with the greatest interest, & find myself convinced on the main point, though I stumble at the eye. How can so perfect an organ have been built up by insensible degrees? I cannot get over the difficulty.

We have had a wretched cold spring here, & my wife has been unwell these three weeks, though she mends now. The garden is a fortnight behind.

Pray tell me also whether you have had any success with the seeds in salt water, as I have a mind to try the experiment myself.

Ever yours sincerely | J. D. Hooker

conversation.partner: a correspondent who presses you hard
turns: Mr Darwin — you spent twenty years gathering facts before publishing, and only then because Wallace forced your hand. I say delay is mostly cowardice dressed as rigour. Convince me otherwise.
That is a comfortable answer, but it does not meet my objection. You had the essential idea in 1838. Twenty years is not caution, it is fear of Owen and the parsons. Admit it.
Then we agree that you were afraid.
Good. And since we agree on that, would you also grant that your whole method — this slow heaping of facts — was mistaken from the start?
I am glad you see it my way at last.
